review_note: Compact objects in D(A) of a Grothendieck abelian category generated by S with each Hom(E,−) coproduct-preserving lie in the retract closure of finite S-complexes. Based on an independent mathematical comparison to the pinned original theorem excerpt in the Stage A record; source proofs/remarks not opened. Preliminary only.
statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The hypothesis is about an arbitrary **Grothendieck abelian category A**, not an O-module category. The set S consists of objects E with Hom_A(E,−) preserving coproducts; every A-object is a quotient of a sum of members of S.

Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a Grothendieck abelian category. Let
$S \subset \Ob(\mathcal{A})$ be a set of objects such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item any object of $\mathcal{A}$ is a quotient of a direct sum
of elements of $S$, and
\item for any $E \in S$ the functor $\Hom_\mathcal{A}(E, -)$
commutes with direct sums.
\end{enumerate}
Then every compact object of $D(\mathcal{A})$ is a direct summand
in $D(\mathcal{A})$ of a finite complex of finite direct sums of
elements of $S$.
hypotheses: A is a Grothendieck abelian category.
S⊂Ob(A) is a set such that each A-object is a quotient of a coproduct of elements of S.
For every E∈S, Hom_A(E,−) commutes with all direct sums.
conclusions: Every compact object of D(A) is a **direct summand in D(A)** of a finite complex whose terms are finite direct sums of objects from S.

\label{lemma-compact-in-terms-of-generators}
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a Grothendieck abelian category. Let
$S \subset \Ob(\mathcal{A})$ be a set of objects such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item any object of $\mathcal{A}$ is a quotient of a direct sum
of elements of $S$, and
\item for any $E \in S$ the functor $\Hom_\mathcal{A}(E, -)$
commutes with direct sums.
\end{enumerate}
Then every compact object of $D(\mathcal{A})$ is a direct summand
in $D(\mathcal{A})$ of a finite complex of finite direct sums of
elements of $S$.

review_note: Finite cofinal coverings by a stable basis guarantee j_{U!}O_U is compact relative to bounded-below sums. Based on an independent mathematical comparison to the pinned original theorem excerpt in the Stage A record; source proofs/remarks not opened. Preliminary only.
statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The selected covers Cov form a **finite cofinal system** for every U∈B, with all finite iterated fibre products remaining in B; this condition, not mere quasi-compactness of U, is the source hypothesis.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site
with set of coverings $\text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$.
Let $\mathcal{B} \subset \Ob(\mathcal{C})$, and
$\text{Cov} \subset \text{Cov}_\mathcal{C}$
be subsets. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item For every $\mathcal{U} \in \text{Cov}$ we have
$\mathcal{U} = \{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$ with $I$ finite,
$U, U_i \in \mathcal{B}$ and every
$U_{i_0} \times_U \ldots \times_U U_{i_p} \in \mathcal{B}$.
\item For every $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the coverings of $U$
occurring in $\text{Cov}$ is a cofinal system of coverings of $U$.
\end{enumerate}
Then for $U \in \mathcal{B}$ the object $j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U$ is
a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$ in the following sense:
if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ in $D(\mathcal{O})$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U, M) =
\bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(j_{U!}\mathcal{O}_U, M_i)$.
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site, B⊂Ob(C), and Cov is a selection of its covering families.
Every cover in Cov is finite, its target/members and all iterated fibre products lie in B.
For each U∈B, the selected Cov-covers of U are cofinal among all coverings of U.
conclusions: For every U∈B, j_{U!}O_U has the **bounded-below** compactness property: Hom(j_{U!}O_U,⊕_iM_i)≅⊕_iHom(j_{U!}O_U,M_i) whenever the sum is bounded below.

review_note: Finite cohomological dimension of U plus direct-sum commutation of all objectwise H^p makes j_{U!}O_U compact in unbounded D(O). Based on an independent mathematical comparison to the pinned original theorem excerpt in the Stage A record; source proofs/remarks not opened. Preliminary only.
statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. Now full compactness in unbounded D(O) follows because there is **one uniform finite cohomological-dimension bound d for the object U**, in addition to preservation of sums.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Let $U$ be an object of
$\mathcal{C}$. The $\mathcal{O}$-module $j_!\mathcal{O}_U$ is a
compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$ if there exists an integer $d$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $H^p(U, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for all $p > d$, and
\item the functors $\mathcal{F} \mapsto H^p(U, \mathcal{F})$
commute with direct sums.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site and U∈C.
There exists integer d with H^p(U,F)=0 for every O-module F and all p>d.
For each p≥0, H^p(U,−) commutes with arbitrary direct sums.
conclusions: j_{U!}O_U is compact in the unbounded derived category D(O).

review_note: Perfect complex is compact relative to bounded-below direct sums under stated qc-covering topology, and fully compact under finite cohomological dimension. Based on an independent mathematical comparison to the pinned original theorem excerpt in the Stage A record; source proofs/remarks not opened. Preliminary only.
statement:
In a triangulated derived category D(A), a **compact object** K is one for which Hom(K,⊕_i M_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i) for **arbitrary** families. A distinct bounded-below-only compactness property is used in D^+(O): it is tested only on direct sums M=⊕ M_i that are bounded below as a whole. For a site object U, j_{U!}O_U is extension by zero from the ringed slice, and its representability relates Hom to derived sections over U. The site hypotheses are exactly (i) quasi-compact **final object X**, (ii) finite cofinal coverings of every quasi-compact object by quasi-compact objects, (iii) quasi-compact pairwise fibre products inside such finite covers. These imply **bounded-below** compactness for perfect K; an **additional** finite cohomological dimension of the final object X is required for compactness in the full unbounded category.

Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Assume
$\mathcal{C}$ has the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{C}$ has a quasi-compact final object $X$,
\item every quasi-compact object of $\mathcal{C}$
has a cofinal system of coverings which are finite
and consist of quasi-compact objects,
\item for a finite covering $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
with $U$, $U_i$ quasi-compact the fibre products $U_i \times_U U_j$ are
quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O})$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $K$ is a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$
in the following sense: if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(K, M) = \bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(K, M_i)$.
\item[(b)] If $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$
has finite cohomological dimension, i.e., if there exists
a $d$ such that $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $i > d$ for
any $\mathcal{O}$-module $\mathcal{F}$, then
$K$ is a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: (C,O) is a ringed site with quasi-compact final object X.
Every quasi-compact site object has a cofinal system of **finite** covers by quasi-compact objects.
For such a finite cover with quasi-compact target and members, U_i×_U U_j is quasi-compact for all i,j.
conclusions: For every family (M_i) with ⊕_iM_i bounded below, Hom(K,⊕_iM_i)≅⊕_iHom(K,M_i).
**If additionally** there is d with H^i(X,F)=0 for all i>d and all O-module sheaves F, then K is compact in unbounded D(O).

\label{lemma-perfect-is-compact}
Let $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$ be a ringed site. Assume
$\mathcal{C}$ has the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{C}$ has a quasi-compact final object $X$,
\item every quasi-compact object of $\mathcal{C}$
has a cofinal system of coverings which are finite
and consist of quasi-compact objects,
\item for a finite covering $\{U_i \to U\}_{i \in I}$
with $U$, $U_i$ quasi-compact the fibre products $U_i \times_U U_j$ are
quasi-compact.
\end{enumerate}
Let $K$ be a perfect object of $D(\mathcal{O})$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] $K$ is a compact object of $D^+(\mathcal{O})$
in the following sense: if $M = \bigoplus_{i \in I} M_i$ is
bounded below, then $\Hom(K, M) = \bigoplus_{i \in I} \Hom(K, M_i)$.
\item[(b)] If $(\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{O})$
has finite cohomological dimension, i.e., if there exists
a $d$ such that $H^i(X, \mathcal{F}) = 0$ for $i > d$ for
any $\mathcal{O}$-module $\mathcal{F}$, then
$K$ is a compact object of $D(\mathcal{O})$.
\end{enumerate}
